text: This made me remember the Japanese restaurant which works on the opposite principle: robotic chefs and human waiters. Video here: [VIDEO] There is an interesting cultural dimension to Germans choosing to replace human interaction with robot interaction while Japanese choosing to replace human work with robot work.

story: Will this robot replace assembly line workers?
text: Not without vision. You'd have to place all the tools and ingredients within reach at precisely known positions, probably all held in a special rig (like this: [VIDEO] ). If something went wrong the robot wouldn't know and would continue executing the recipe with possibly disastrous results. Robots won't be replacing chefs until visual feedback is solved.

story: Robot Baristas Serve Up the Future of Coffee at Cafe X
